correctness.rationale: The three-vector frame is exactly Parseval. For the explicit one-parameter family, direct multiplication gives T_Lambda V_c=K and V_c^*V_c=diag(1,1/4+c^2). Thus every |c|<=sqrt(3)/2 is a distinct dual of norm one. Since ||K||=||T_Lambda||=1, every solution has norm at least one. The kernel computation identifies the reduced Douglas solution exactly.

value.rationale: The proposition is used to define the canonical controlled K-g-dual through a purported uniqueness property. The counterexample shows a continuum, not an isolated second minimizer, even for an invertible K and an ordinary Parseval frame. It also gives a precise repair: retain the Douglas reduced-range condition to recover genuine uniqueness.
